name: Battle of Aljubarrota
summary: At the Battle of Aljubarrota (August 14, 1385), John I of Portugal, the illegitimate son of Peter I, championed by Portuguese merchants and commoners against the Castilian-backed nobility, defeats a substantially larger Castilian army under Juan I of Castile. The Portuguese position on a prepared ridge with ditches, combined with English longbowmen from the Lancaster alliance (João had married Philippa of Lancaster), repels Castilian cavalry charges in a pattern reminiscent of Crécy. Juan I escapes; the Castilian claim to Portugal is finished. The Aviz dynasty is secured; Portugal's independence is guaranteed for two centuries.

_quarry.structural_significance: Secures Portuguese independence from Castilian annexation; establishes the Aviz dynasty; the English alliance (formalized in the Treaty of Windsor 1386) provides the foundation for England's oldest alliance, still technically in force; Portugal's independence enables the age of exploration
